scenes.text: In nineteen fifty-four, a rock from space crashed through a roof and hit a sleeping woman.
Her name was Ann Hodges, and she was napping on her couch in Alabama.
It happened on November thirtieth, near the town of Sylacauga.
The meteorite punched a hole through the ceiling and smashed her big wooden radio.
Then it bounced and slammed into her, leaving a huge bruise on her hip and hand.
The rock weighed about eight and a half pounds.
People in parts of three states saw a fireball streak across the sky.
Many of them thought a plane had crashed.
By nightfall, crowds of reporters and sightseers packed her yard.
The Air Force took the rock away to confirm it really came from space.
Then her landlady sued, claiming the rock was hers, and they settled out of court.
The next day, a farmer found a second piece and sold it for enough to buy a car and a home.
Ann donated her rock to the Alabama Museum of Natural History, where it's still on display.
She's still the only person known to have been hit by a meteorite.
Would you keep the meteorite, or sell it? Tell me below.

title: The only person ever known to be hit by a meteorite ☄️
caption: On Nov 30, 1954, an 8.5-pound meteorite crashed through Ann Hodges' roof in Alabama, smashed her radio and bruised her as she napped. She's still the only person known to have been hit by one.
